name: Gate Sword Primer (Sơn Môn Kiếm Quyết)
concept: The grey sisters' method, taught at the Gate Hermitage. It draws the mountain's Metal qi into a short, upright sword that is drilled for one purpose: to stand in a doorway and not be moved. Its forms all face one way, downhill. It never cultivates Ice, and the grey sisters know it: it is a guard's method, and they are the hermitage's guard.
lore: Written by the founder Kỷ Hoa Ảnh in 702, the year she sealed the cave above the hermitage, so that the women at the gate could hold it without her.

name: Pear Blossom Snow Sword (Lê Hoa Tuyết Kiếm)
concept: The white nuns' sword, made from the night in 600 when snow fell like pear blossom in the eighth month (A103). The blade throws off a drift of frost petals that hang in the air. A foe moving through them gathers Ice stacks, and a nun standing in them moves more lightly. It is slow to learn and gentle to watch, and those who have fought it say it is like being buried.
lore: Only white nuns learn it. A grey sister who awakens Ice is taught it on the night she takes the white robe. Its first forms are the first six layers of Hoắc Hàn Quang's North Wind, Cold Light Sword, which the founder learned from him (hermits-sages; settled in the cross-sect pass).

name: Sealed Cold Sutra (Phong Hàn Kinh)
concept: The founder's seal method. It teaches how to close a place with cold so that nothing, qi, sound or a sword's light, passes out of it, and how to renew the seal by sitting against it for a season. It is the art that has kept Hoắc Hàn Quang's cave shut since 700 (C014). In a fight it lays cold seals on a foe's arts: each seal slows one art, and the fourth stills them all for a breath.
lore: Taught only to the abbess and the one nun who walks with her to the seal every fifty years. Thái Lê Tuyết has not chosen the next one.
